title: Sigil and Ember
premise: Mara Quintana, exiled from her storm-calling order for refusing to weaponize her gift, has spent seven years guiding smugglers through the Thornfell mountains while hiding the ember-sigil burned into her palm. When a dying courier presses a bloodstained map into her hands, she learns it leads to the Ember Vault, where an ancient war-storm sleeps, and that the sigil on her hand is the only key to opening or destroying it. Hunted by both her former order and a rising warlord who wants the vault opened, Mara gathers an unlikely found family of smugglers, defrocked priests, and one stubborn knight sent to kill her. In the end, Mara chooses belonging over exile: she shatters the vault with a storm called not in anger but in love, sacrificing her power to save her companions, and finally comes home to people rather than a place.
about_author: Jonah Hartwell is the pen name of a former mountain guide turned novelist who writes fantasy about outsiders finding their way home. Sigil and Ember is his third novel, following the acclaimed The Saltbound Road.

chapters.title: The Road That Remembers
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She guides a smuggler caravan through a blizzard she secretly calms, establishing her hidden power and careful invisibility. A stranger's body is found frozen on the pass. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence; Mara believes safety means being no one.

chapters.title: A Dying Man's Bargain
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The frozen stranger, half-alive, presses a bloodstained map into her hands and whispers 'the vault wakes' before dying. His pursuers arrive at the inn asking questions. Emotional beat: dread; Mara realizes her anonymity has just died with him.

chapters.title: What the Map Shows
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, with interludes of the map's shifting ink. She deciphers enough to learn it points beneath Thornfell itself, and that her palm-sigil burns hotter near it. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity warring with the instinct to burn the map and run.

chapters.title: Knights in Grey Wool
chapters.summary: Ser Aldric Vane's POV. He arrives in the border town hunting the courier's killer, carrying orders to retrieve the map and execute its bearer if marked. He glimpses Mara and hesitates. Emotional beat: duty beginning to chafe against conscience.

chapters.title: Smoke Over Lowmarket
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Warlord Kessrin's soldiers torch the smuggler quarter searching for the map; Mara's mentor Bren is captured. She flees with only the map and Bren's daughter, Pip. Emotional beat: guilt and fury; invisibility has cost her everything she pretended not to love.

chapters.title: The Company of Strays
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In a waystation, she falls in with odd allies: defrocked priest Odessa, gambler twins Sef and Illo, and gruff dwarf mason Torv. First hints of found family forming around a shared fire. Emotional beat: warmth she doesn't trust yet.

chapters.title: Storms Answer to No One
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Ambushed by Kessrin's riders, Mara unleashes her storm-calling openly for the first time in years, saving the company but revealing herself. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into fear; she can never hide again.

chapters.title: The Order's Long Shadow
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Mara's POV. Seven years earlier: her trial before the storm-caller order, her refusal to bind storms into weapons, her exile and the burning of the sigil into her palm. Emotional beat: understanding why she chose exile, and what it truly cost.

chapters.title: A Knight Off His Leash
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. He catches up to Mara alone at a shrine, blade drawn, but she shows him the map and the truth about the vault. He lets her go and burns his orders. Emotional beat: the first act of chosen loyalty; two exiles recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Beneath the Thornfell Roots
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The company descends into abandoned dwarven tunnels guided by Torv, pursued by both Kessrin's army and Mara's former order's hunters. Emotional beat: claustrophobic tension broken by small acts of trust between companions.

chapters.title: The Vault Wakes
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. They reach the Ember Vault's outer gate; the sigil flares, and distant horizons darken as the sleeping war-storm stirs. Odessa reveals the order built the vault to imprison a storm-god they once worshipped. Emotional beat: awe and horror; the secret is bigger than any of them.

chapters.title: Kessrin's Offer
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Kessrin captures Pip and offers a trade: the sigil-key for the girl. Mara considers surrendering the world's fate for one child. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh—love against duty, and what each is worth.

chapters.title: The Price of One Small Life
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The exchange goes wrong; Sef dies buying Pip's escape. The company fractures, some blaming Mara's softness, others her hesitation. Emotional beat: grief and recrimination; found family tested by loss.

chapters.title: What Odessa Buried
chapters.summary: Odessa's POV. She confesses she was the order's vault-keeper who fled decades ago, and that the sigil isn't just a key—it's a leash, and whoever holds it becomes the storm's vessel. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as protection; Mara learns her exile was engineered.

chapters.title: The Order Comes Home
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Her former mentor, Archon Veyra, arrives—not to kill her, but to beg her to open the vault so the order can control the god within. Mara refuses. Emotional beat: the past offering a seductive lie of purpose and home.

chapters.title: Emberlight
chapters.summary: Mara and Aldric's shared POV. On the eve of battle, quiet scenes: Aldric tending Mara's burning sigil-hand, confessions exchanged, the company mending its rifts around a fire. Emotional beat: tenderness; love declared plainly in the shadow of doom.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Pass
chapters.summary: Battle chapter, rotating POVs. Kessrin's army and the order's hunters converge on the vault gate; the company holds the tunnel mouth. Torv collapses the pass behind them, sealing everyone in together. Emotional beat: desperate courage; every companion choosing to stay.

chapters.title: Vessel
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Inside the vault, the war-storm offers Mara unlimited power if she opens fully to it—the exile's dream of mattering. Veyra takes the power instead and begins to transform. Emotional beat: temptation refused; Mara sees clearly what she does and doesn't want.

chapters.title: The Storm Called in Love
chapters.summary: Climax, Mara's POV. As Veyra-as-storm tears the mountain apart, Mara calls a counter-storm—not through rage but through every bond she's forged, letting the company anchor her. She shatters the vault and unmakes the war-storm, burning out her own power. Emotional beat: transcendence through connection; duty fulfilled by love, not obedience.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Ash
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. He digs Mara from the rubble, alive but stormless, her sigil gone grey. Kessrin is dead, the order scattered, the war averted without anyone knowing. Emotional beat: exhausted relief; grief for the power that was part of her.

chapters.title: No Longer No One
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The company rebuilds Lowmarket's smuggler quarter together; Odessa stays as its keeper, Torv reopens the tunnels, Pip declares herself Mara's apprentice. Mara grieves her storms and finds she doesn't need them to be whole. Emotional beat: healing; identity rebuilt on people instead of power.

chapters.title: Sigil and Ember
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Mara's POV. Spring returns to Thornfell. Mara and Aldric walk the high passes she once walked alone, now as guides leading a found family homeward. Her scarred palm aches only when storms gather far away—and she smiles. Emotional beat: belonging earned; the exile finally home.
